panels.description: Wide. A lamplit room in the fort. Nagoji at a low writing table stacked with string-bound palm-leaf bundles, reading one leaf. The corner of his moustache lifts, very slightly.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some months after Colachel, and before fire ever touched Padmini's upper fields, things shifted between Revathi and me.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A message on canal rights, addressed to me and not to Ramayyan's office. A question about horse breeds among the levy schedules.

panels.description: Wide, full page width. Dusk at a village temple near the Velinadu border: a sloping tiled Kerala roof, a tall brass lamp-pillar, a procession of women in white carrying brass lamps, *chenda* drummers behind them. Nagoji at the edge of the crowd. Across the courtyard, near the offering stones, Revathi in her indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, flat-coin necklace, a few threads of grey in her hair, no tali.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Then an invitation. My presence was required for security.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: No one there needed securing.

panels.description: Insert, tight. A plate of *prasadam* on a banana leaf. Two RIGHT hands reaching for it at the same moment: his, ridged nails, the edge of his cream shoulder cloth near the wrist (no brand in this insert; the brand is on his left wrist, out of frame); hers, gold bangles. The fingers touch. Neither hand moves away.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She was there to inspect the local granaries. That was the fiction.

panels.description: The two of them side by side watching the procession, not looking at each other. Lamplight on both faces.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You are far from your marches.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The marches can spare me for a day.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Only a day?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Perhaps two.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Morning sky over the temple roof and the coconut palms. Two hawks circling on the same column of air. Far below, tiny, two figures walking the same path by the temple tank from opposite ends.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was two days, and then three.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We did not speak of what we were doing, circling each other like two hawks who had spotted the same thermal.

panels.description: Third evening. The edge of the village, the festival breaking up behind them, lamps being carried home. Revathi's mounted escort waits in the road. She has stopped. He has stopped.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: This cannot continue.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: No.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: It is noticed. People talk. Ramayyan has already written three lines about it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Only three?

panels.description: Close on Revathi. She does not smile.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Come to Velinadu. When you are ready to speak plainly.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Not before.

panels.description: Wide. She rides away with her escort into the dusk and does not look back. Nagoji alone at the village edge, small, the last festival lamps behind him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It took me two months to find the courage.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A dozen reasons why a landless Maratha and a Princess of Velinadu belonged in different stories. Each one crumbled when I remembered her hand.

panels.description: Padmini's yard, under the jackfruit tree. Padmini (fifties, black hair coiled at the nape, cotton sari hitched for walking, long stick) holds out a folded cloth dyed deep green. Her fingers linger on its edge as he takes it.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: She asks. Not commands.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: That is already different.

panels.description: Insert, tight. The green cloth open across his palms. A few lines of fine stitching, drawn as abstract embroidery with NO legible script (reserve space; the message is lettered as a caption styled like thread).

copy.speaker: CAPTION (stitched lettering)
copy.text: *Come to Velinadu when the next moon is full. There is a decision to be made that cannot be written.*

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was not signed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It did not need to be.

panels.description: Wide, full page width. Late afternoon, a pale full moon rising over the palms. The Velinadu house compound: thicker laterite walls than before, men with muskets at the gate where there used to be only spears, children in the courtyards. Nagoji arriving on foot, leading Kayal, his bay mare.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Velinadu had changed since my first visit.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Yet the bones of the place remained the same.

panels.description: The inner courtyard and the long verandah. In the background, the kalari pit: boys moving with sticks while their sisters watch and comment. Revathi stands under a carved wooden beam, inclining her head the smallest fraction. The same few grey threads as at the festival (1.2); no tali.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Ananthan Pillai.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Or do you still answer to Nagoji when you dream?

panels.description: Nagoji, dry.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Depends on the dream.

panels.description: Tight on Revathi. Her mouth twitches.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You have not grown less infuriating.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. The two of them walking the length of the verandah without speaking, in low late-afternoon light. The household moves around them: a woman's bangled wrists, a pestle pounding grain, a boy mid-shout in the kalari. At the end of the verandah she has stopped at a pillar, one hand resting on it, and is turning to face him fully.
Revathi at the pillar, straight-backed, formal.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: My uncles bring proposals every week. Men of good lineage. Men with land. Men whose feet are firmly planted in this red soil.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: They promise safety.

panels.description: Nagoji, a half step back, watching her.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And yet you sent a green cloth to a landless Maratha.

panels.description: A ghost of a smile touches her lips.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Because safety bores me.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: But fear does not.

panels.description: She takes a step closer, searching his face. The distance between them is the whole panel.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I am afraid, Nagoji. Not of war. Of you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Me?

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Revathi's face in the foreground, speaking. Behind her, bleeding into the panel edge like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame: dry brown Deccan hills, a dust road running north, a lone rider going away up it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: If I marry you, will you stay true?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Or will you one day wake, smell the dust of the north, and ride back to your hills, leaving me with memories and ghosts?

panels.description: She has let go of the pillar and walks on down the verandah. Nagoji keeps pace at her side, steady, looking ahead, not at her.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The Deccan is my past. You are my present.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Present is fleeting. And there is another thing. A harder thing.

panels.description: Passing the open door of the council room: inside, the elders' mats lie empty. A guard with a musket at the door straightens as she passes. Revathi's chin lifting. The matriarch, not the lover.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That lift of her chin always made my breath catch.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I am not a woman who walks three paces behind. I am the matriarch of Velinadu. I sit in councils. I command men.

panels.description: Tight on her eyes, gold light from the council-room lattice falling across them.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Can you, a warrior who has ridden with kings, accept a woman as his equal?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Not in the shadows. In the light.

panels.description: Nagoji, stopped at the threshold of the council room, one hand on the door frame. A small smile.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I have ridden with Padmini Amma. I know what a woman with iron in her spine looks like.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Inside the council room, shot from behind Revathi: her dark silhouette in the foreground, unmoved, one hand resting on the back of the matriarch's low carved seat at the head of the empty mats. Across the room, small in the bright doorway, Nagoji.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Padmini is your mother by oath. I would be your wife. It is different.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: A husband expects to rule. Here, you will not rule.

panels.description: Wide. From the courtyard steps she gestures at the house around them as the evening lamps are lit: grandmothers on a raised platform, young women at the grain, a girl touching a flame to a tall brass lamp, girls watching the kalari, a small child on a hip. Women everywhere at the centre of it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: This is *Marumakkathayam*, Nagoji. The lineage runs through the women.

panels.description: The two of them, mid-shot on the steps, lamplight coming up on their faces, the courtyard behind.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: If we have children, sons or daughters, they will belong to Velinadu. Of my house, not yours.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You will be the father, loved and honoured. But you will be a visitor in their heritage.

panels.description: Close on Revathi, lamplit. This is the real question and she knows it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Can your pride accept that? Can you watch your son grow up belonging to a world where you are always, in some small way, a guest?

panels.description: Nagoji looking down at the stone step under their feet. Hold on him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought of the pride of my ancestors, the patrilineal certainty of the Marathas.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. He looks up at her. Quiet.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: My pride died at Colachel. It was reborn as something else.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Something that values the root over the branch.

panels.description: Nagoji leaning on the stable rail beside Kayal, his bay mare, speaking plainly.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will always be a guest here.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If you can spare me a corner of your house and a sliver of your heart, that is enough.

panels.description: Revathi at the rail, lantern light on her face. Her eyes close, briefly.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You already hold more than a sliver. But I have responsibilities.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You are an honoured guest here, and a guest under Padmanabha's sky. This land was never yours to own. Only to serve.

panels.description: Nagoji spreads his empty hands. Kayal pushes her nose into his open palms, looking for something that is not there.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: My own house is a neem in the fort courtyard and a jackfruit in Padmini's yard.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: My only property is a horse that does not like cannon smoke.

panels.description: Revathi smiles, genuinely this time. Behind them two small nieces run past the stable, bickering over something clutched in one girl's fist.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Then you lose nothing you truly possess.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And gain nieces who will argue with you and sons who will pretend to listen.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Soft-edged, warm, a picture in his head: small bare feet running on the courtyard stones; a child's hand, sticky with fruit, tugging his toward the kalari; Revathi in the background with one finger raised, scolding him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The picture that rose in my mind undid me more than any flattery could have.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Her voice, scolding me for teaching them dirty Deccan curses.

panels.description: Under the carved beam, the moon over the courtyard behind them. Nagoji, a little unsteady.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Padmini knows?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: She was the one who told me to stop being proud and send for you.

panels.description: Inset, soft-edged: Revathi's telling of a recent scene, within the last two months. Padmini's yard under the jackfruit tree. Padmini, stick planted, jabbing a finger at Revathi, who stands with her arms folded. Revathi exactly as she is in this chapter, NOT younger: indigo sari, flat-coin necklace, the same few grey threads, no tali.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: She said, "If you must refuse him, do it with a full stomach, not an empty bed."

panels.description: Nagoji laughing, head back. Revathi startled by the sound.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And Ramayyan?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: He has already written three lines about the possible outcomes. He will adjust the fourth when we tell him what we have decided.

panels.description: Nagoji, serious again, the two of them close.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: My name in the Deccan is already a ghost. If I marry you, I do not become lord of Velinadu. I become another story whispered in its corridors.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Yes. One more story. One more thread in the cloth. That is all any of us are.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. He steps closer. Their faces in profile under the carved beam, the moon behind them.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then let it be written.

panels.description: Revathi lets out a breath she has been holding.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Do not expect wedding songs. We are too old for that nonsense.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You are. I, on the other hand, am ageless.

panels.description: She snorts and turns brisk, the commander again, counting points off on her fingers. He is trying not to grin.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You will sleep in the small room near the western verandah. Morning rites when you are here. Drills when you are not.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You will not teach our nieces to gamble with cowrie shells.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I make no promises about the cowries.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Their hands at their sides, brushing. This time neither hand pretends.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The same light touch as on that verandah after the Dutch bowed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: This time, neither of us pretended not to feel it.

panels.description: Wide, full page width. The wedding day. The Velinadu courtyard being prepared: garlands being strung, brass vessels polished, *chenda* and *thimila* drummers tuning under the eaves. House elders. No courtiers.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The marriage itself was smaller than any court scribe would have wanted, and larger than either of us would admit mattered.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Only those who had carried these years with us.

panels.description: The gate, morning. A rider swinging down from a brown horse, caked in road dust, grinning: Dhanaji (stockier and a little shorter than Nagoji, short black beard, white turban, long-sleeved indigo tunic to the knee, cream trousers, riding boots, plain leather sword belt, no sash, talwar). Nagoji turning toward him: bare-headed, topknot, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, the conch knife at his waist.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Dhanaji. A grin I had not seen since we were young men racing horses on the Deccan plateau.

panels.description: The forearm clasp in the courtyard, both men laughing. Dhanaji is already looking past Nagoji's shoulder at the garlands being strung and the brass being polished. The conch knife at Nagoji's waist.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: You could have sent word earlier. I had to bribe three boatmen and outride a tax collector to get here.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Revathi does not believe in long engagements.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: So. The last of us to fall.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You never fell.

panels.description: Dhanaji's grin gone. He looks at the floor, scuffing the toe of his riding boot against the stone. Nagoji watching him, the knife still at his waist.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: I am going back. To the Deccan. I miss my parents. I miss the dry air.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: I am not of this place, Ananthan. I am homesick.

panels.description: Inset, tight. Two hands that must read as two different men: Nagoji's RIGHT hand on a bare forearm, ridged nails, pressing the knife into Dhanaji's palm; Dhanaji's hand coming out of a dusty indigo sleeve cuff, fingers already pushing back. The knife: straight narrow blade, ivory handle, gold at guard and pommel, the conch stamped near the hilt.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: No. I will not carry a foreign king's treasure. It suits you here.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am tying myself to this coast. Take it, Dhanaji.

panels.description: Nagoji closing Dhanaji's fingers over the knife with both hands, the brand showing on his LEFT wrist. Above the hands, Dhanaji's face under the white turban, swallowing.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You are the one man who remembers the Deccan boy under my skin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If the gods cut you down, let your son come south with it. Let him find me by the conch and the gold. I will not turn him away.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Dhanaji slides the knife into his sword belt under the hem of his tunic, hiding the gold like contraband, his hand staying on it. Nagoji's waist bare of any knife.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: You swear that?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I swear it.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: If anyone asks, I stole it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If anyone asks, tell them you earned it.

panels.description: Wide, full page width. The courtyard as the sun touches the tops of the coconut palms. Padmini large in the left foreground, just behind Revathi's shoulder, three-quarter view, looking at Nagoji: her finest white, jasmine in her coiled hair, stick planted, eyes bright. Mid-ground: the sacred fire; Revathi seated before it; Nagoji kneeling at her right; the priest across the fire, facing them. At the back of the courtyard, small and readable by costume only, left to right: De Lannoy (tall, pale hair tied back, white cotton coat over a white mundu, no blue anywhere); Ponnan and two of his men (curly hair loose, red shoulder cloths, short jackets); Dhanaji leaning on the far wall, arms crossed (white turban, indigo tunic).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: When Padmini looked at me, I saw not just approval but something like completion.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: As if a circle she had been drawing for years had finally closed.

panels.description: The priest, across the fire from the couple, holding up the *tali*: a small gold pendant on a yellow thread, water and ash still on his fingers. Temple-priest face as in the page note. In the near foreground, the edge of Nagoji's plain white shoulder cloth and his moustached profile, so the two men read as two.

copy.speaker: PRIEST
copy.text: Take it. Tie it, and she is yours. She ties her thread to you, and you are hers.

copy.speaker: PRIEST
copy.text: Three knots for three lives. Past, present, and what is yet to come.

panels.description: Revathi, looking not at the priest or the fire but straight at him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The same question she had asked on the verandah.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: *Can you do this? Can you stay?*

panels.description: Insert, tight. The *tali* lying in his cupped palms.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had held swords and reins and dying men.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had never held anything that felt as heavy as this small piece of metal.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Revathi bows her head. Her braid is pinned up, so the nape of her neck is bare. On the nape, just below the back hairline, a small pale scar, drawn clearly.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Something I had never noticed in all our nights in the cellar. A story I did not yet know.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I would have time to learn it now.

panels.description: His hands bringing the yellow thread around her neck. They are trembling; draw it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had charged Dutch squares without flinching.

copy.speaker: PRIEST (off)
copy.text: For the past. For all that brought you to this moment.

panels.description: Narrow strip, three images bleeding into each other like stains: a hand going under a black storm wave; the brand on his LEFT wrist; a brass lamp on the floor of a low cellar.
The second knot. Revathi reaches up, not to adjust the thread, but to press his hand briefly.

copy.speaker: PRIEST (off)
copy.text: For the present. For what you are to each other now.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Telling me without words that this was real. That I was not dreaming in some fever after Colachel.

panels.description: Tight. The third knot pulled tight, his fingers, the yellow thread, the gold.

copy.speaker: PRIEST (off)
copy.text: For what is yet to come. For children and grandchildren. For the thread that continues after you are both dust.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Revathi lifts her head and looks at him. Her eyes are wet. The *tali* at her throat from this panel on, in every panel for the rest of the book: a small gold pendant on its yellow thread, worn high at the throat, clearly separate from the longer flat-coin necklace.

copy.speaker: PRIEST (off)
copy.text: It is done.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Something I had never seen her permit herself to show in public.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: Hope.

panels.description: Wide. The drums louder, triumphant. Women ululating. Dhanaji (white turban, indigo tunic) whooping with a fist in the air like a boy at a horse fair. At the centre the couple sit still, looking only at each other, the *tali* at her throat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I heard none of it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was looking at my wife. My *wife*.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a moment the world was only the two of us and the thin gold thread that now bound us.

panels.description: Close, two heads bent together.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You did not drop it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I almost did.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I know. I felt your hands shaking. The great cavalry commander, terrified of a piece of string.

panels.description: Nagoji, honest. Revathi with the private smile.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The string is easy. It is what it means that terrifies me.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Good. Stay terrified. It will keep you honest.

panels.description: Wide, full page width. The feast: banana leaves lining the courtyard floor, rice in small mountains, curries around them, *pappadam*, pickled mango, and brass vessels of *avial* arriving in steam. Fixed seating: Nagoji cross-legged at his leaf, Revathi on his right (tali visible), Padmini on his left, leaning toward him. Across the row of leaves, Ramayyan (thin, receding hair, plain white) methodically mixing his rice with his fingers, not looking up.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Ramayyan invented this. During a siege, when we had many vegetables and little else.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He told the cooks to combine everything and pray.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You invented a dish?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I solved a logistics problem. The cooks merely executed.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Close on Nagoji's right hand at his leaf, mixing rice and curry into a small ball, coconut oil slick on his palm. Beside him, Revathi laughing, unguarded, the *tali* at her throat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a moment I forgot that I was a Maratha in a Nair house, a sword in a land of pepper.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was simply a hungry man at a wedding feast.

panels.description: Wide. The western verandah at night. Revathi sitting with her back against a pillar, watching the courtyard; Nagoji beside her. Behind them, through an open door, the house shrine, wordless: a small bronze Bhagavathi in a wall niche and a tiered brass lamp, its flames burning steady. No temple, no large idol.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Do you feel married?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I feel like a guest who has been told he may stay past sunset.

panels.description: Revathi, turning to him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Good. Never forget you are that. When you ride out, you carry my name now.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You carry the children we may have. Do not make them spit when they say "Ananthan Pillai."

panels.description: Her profile. Below, in the courtyard, a single lamp flame gutters and steadies.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: My mother died when I was young. Sometimes I try to remember her face and find only the lines other people drew for me.

panels.description: Nagoji takes her hand. She lets him, still looking out at the courtyard.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I do not want our children to know me only as a name in Ramayyan's leaves.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: They will know me as the woman who sent their father to the marches. Do not let them hate me for that.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. She is already rising, her hand held out to him. He is still seated, looking up at her.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If they must hate anyone, let it be me. I will tell them it was my choice to ride. Yours to keep the roof over their heads.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Come.

panels.description: Wide. A heavy carved teak door pushed open. Inside, a single lamp. A low bed spread with white cloth and strewn with jasmine.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: No cellar tonight. No hiding. You are my husband now. This is your room as much as mine.

panels.description: Revathi taking off her jewellery, the heavy gold at her ears, the bangles, setting each piece on a wooden stand. The *tali* stays. Nagoji hovering near the door.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It does not feel like mine.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: It will. Give it time.

panels.description: Her back to him, then half turned.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: In the cellar, we were thieves. Stealing hours.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Tonight we are not thieves. There is nothing to hide from.

panels.description: She reaches up and pulls the pins from the braid coiled at the back of her head. The braid drops and she loosens it; her hair falls, darker than the shadows behind her.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I find I do not know how to do this without hiding. I have been a widow so long that secrecy became a skin.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Help me shed it.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. He crosses to her and takes her face in both hands. His hands are steady now. The lamp behind them.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We learn together.

panels.description: Tight. The lamp flame guttering out on its stand. Jasmine scattered on white cloth.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I learned the scar at her hairline. A fall from a mango tree, when she was seven.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I learned the way she said my real name, *Nagoji*, when she forgot to be careful.

panels.description: Later. Moonlight through a window lattice. Their faces close on the pillow, the white cloth drawn up over both of them to the shoulders, the *tali* at her throat. Her fingertip at the grey on his temple.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You are older.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: So are you.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I have earned it. You have merely survived.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Survival is its own earning.

panels.description: Her head resting on the white cloth over his chest; the cloth stays up to the shoulders and his ribs stay covered. He is already half rising out of old habit; her arm tightens across him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I should go. Before the servants...

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You should stay. You are not a guest anymore, Ananthan. You can be here when the sun rises.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I did not have to leave.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I could stay.

panels.description: Cut away from the bed. The moonlit window lattice; on the sill below it, the cold lamp and a few fallen jasmine flowers. No figures. The three balloons come out of the dark, their tails running off panel toward the bed.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: It will take time to stop feeling like a thief.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: It took me years to stop feeling like a widow. We are both haunted. But perhaps haunted people can keep each other company.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Company. Yes. I think I can do that.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Dawn light through the lattice. Revathi asleep beside him, the *tali* at her throat, the white cloth to their shoulders. Nagoji asleep on, one hand open and loose near hers, nowhere near a weapon. The waking house is shown, not heard: in the strip of light under the teak door, the shadows of passing feet; through the lattice, small figures of children in the courtyard.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For the first time, I did not wake at the sound of footsteps. For the first time, I did not reach for a weapon.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: For the first time, I was home.

panels.description: Wide, full page width, high angle. Velinadu in the morning: kitchen smoke rising, courtyards filling, the kalari waking. Beyond the walls, the road running away through the palms.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For the first time since Goa, since the dungeon, since the storm, I felt something like rest.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not peace.

panels.description: Nagoji on the western verandah in morning light, looking out past the walls. No knife at his waist.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The world beyond Velinadu still boiled. Mysore still watched. The British and the French still bartered with Arcot. The Dutch still counted their losses.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Travancore still balanced on knives.

panels.description: Revathi comes to stand beside him, the *tali* at her throat, separate from the flat-coin necklace. Her hand finds his without either of them looking down.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But here, in this house where pepper and politics and old love all shared the same air, I was no longer only a sword.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate)
copy.text: I was also a husband.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Soft-edged, a picture of what is to come: children running these stones, one small rider on a pony in the kalari yard, learning to sit a horse.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And, in time, a father whose children ran these stones and called this place home, even as they learned to ride under a king whose kingdom we had both helped, and hindered, and loved into being.
